newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline turns higher with NYMEX, tight barges.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline turns higher with NYMEX, tight barges.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended modestly higher on Wednesday after an upswing in NYMEX futures and continued talk of tighter barge material, traders said.
But a flurry of deals by three players and the recent closure of the arbitrage to the States left many traders cautious of the next move in barges, which rose about $2.

Eurograde barges were last quoted at $190/$193 fob ARA, posting a wide range for the second straight day. Trades started the day at $186 and prompt refinery material was later heard near the day's highs.
Regular unleaded was valued $6 lower at $184/$187, with no deals visibly done.
"There is not too much product available in ARA but there is availability on the cargo front because there is no outlet for NWE," said one barge trader in Germany.
"No one is keen to build up stocks because prices are cheaper later out...but the backwardation means that for the prompt there is not too much available."

NYMEX gasoline, recovering from a more than 2.50 cent loss on Tuesday, rose over a cent by midday in New York. Both American Petroleum Institute and Energy Information Administration data showed gasoline stocks in the U.S. rose about 2.6-2.7 million barrels last week.
The EIA also said that gasoline demand in the latest four-week period was 8.03 million bpd, up a slight 0.2 percent from a year ago.

In central and eastern Europe, demand continues to be quiet, especially out of Poland, said one broker. A cut in domestic Polish prices has made cargoes on the international market too expensive, he said.
"It's been a very disappointing market this year," he said. "Demand downstream in Poland has not been exceptional."
Some short positions for the last decade in June were being covered and fresh Polish demand may emerge in July, he added.
